key_terms.definition: The burnt offering a man brings when he "appears" in the Temple on a pilgrimage festival. Like every olah it is burned entirely on the altar; none of it is eaten.
key_terms.on_this_daf: One of the two festival offerings whose minimum value Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel dispute, and a candidate for the olah offered at Sinai.

key_terms.definition: The peace offering (shelamim) brought on a pilgrimage festival. Parts go on the altar and the owners eat the rest, so it is shared between God and the people.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Beit Hillel make it the costlier festival offering, and argue that it is the offering type that already existed before Sinai.

key_terms.definition: Additional peace offerings eaten in rejoicing on the festival, fulfilling the command to rejoice (simchah). Women are obligated in simchah as well as men.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The mother's obligation in simchah explains how a child reaches Jerusalem at all. R. Yosi HaGlili counts it as the third pilgrimage offering, each with its own distinctive feature.

key_terms.definition: The rabbinic obligation to train a child in the mitzvot he will owe as an adult, starting once he is capable of performing them.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Abaye: chinukh follows what an adult in the child's present condition would owe, so a lame or blind child who may yet heal is exempt now.

key_terms.definition: The communal burnt offering of a lamb, brought every morning and every afternoon in the Temple.
key_terms.on_this_daf: Beit Hillel, R. Akiva and R. Yosi HaGlili identify the olah of Shemot 24:5 as the tamid. The debate is whether it began at Sinai or only in the Mishkan.

key_terms.sense: flaying and cutting up a burnt offering
key_terms.definition: Removing the hide of an olah and cutting it into its prescribed pieces before it is burned on the altar.
key_terms.on_this_daf: For R. Yishmael these procedures were taught only at the Ohel Mo'ed. So an olah offered at Sinai, without them, could not have been the tamid, which requires them.

key_terms.sense: general rules versus details of the Torah's laws
key_terms.definition: The question of which parts of the Torah's laws were given at Sinai: the general rules only (with the details taught later, at the Ohel Mo'ed), or the details as well.
key_terms.on_this_daf: R. Yishmael: the general rules came at Sinai and the details later. R. Akiva: both were given at Sinai, and repeated at the Ohel Mo'ed and at Arvot Mo'av.

key_terms.definition: Mitzvot for which the Torah sets no required amount, listed in the Mishnah at the opening of Pe'ah: pe'ah, bikkurim, re'ayon, acts of kindness and Torah study.
key_terms.on_this_daf: The Gemara asks whether "no measure" for re'ayon rules out a minimum, a maximum, or both.
